Successful OWA/Exchange access within 24h of a password reset (post-rotation mailbox access) AIInstallation Medium
Correlates an Azure AD password reset/change with a subsequent successful sign-in to Office 365 Exchange Online for the same user within 24 hours — the exact 'access survives credential rotation' thesis of the OWAReaper campaign. Surfaces access that should have been invalidated by the reset. Rationale: Directly targets the article's headline claim that 'credential rotation... will not evict the actor' — a successful Exchange Online sign-in inside a 24h window after a password reset for the same UPN is the observable signature of persistence that ignored the rotation. Correlation of AuditLogs reset + SigninLogs success on the Exchange resource keeps it specific. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/cleaning-out-inboxes-ta488-comes-outlook-another-half-click-exploit • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-hackers-exploit-exchange-owa-zero-day-for-long-term-mailbox-access/
ATT&CKT1098.002 T1550
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user resets their own password then immediately signs back into webmail (most common benign case)
  • Help-desk resets a password and the user logs in the same day from a known device/location
  • Session that re-authenticates with a fresh MFA challenge after reset (add MFA filter to suppress)
  • Password-expiry-driven change during an active OWA session on a managed corporate IP
Suppression filter
| where AuthenticationRequirement != "multiFactorAuthentication"
Response runbook
1) Triage: compare the post-reset sign-in IP/geo/device and AuthenticationRequirement against the user's baseline — a single-factor success from an unfamiliar IP is the alarm; a compliant device from a normal location is likely benign. 2) Contain: if suspicious, revoke all refresh tokens (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken), re-reset the password, enforce MFA re-registration, and audit the mailbox for Default/Anonymous folder permissions (server-side persistence the reset can't clear). 3) Hunt: check the source IP for the four OWAReaper C2 domains and for other org accounts signing into the same victim mailbox (delegate access granted by OWAReaper).
let resets = IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("Account Password changed","Account Password reset")
| project ResetTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ResourceDisplayName == "Office 365 Exchange Online"
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where Application has_any ("Outlook","OWA","Exchange")
| join kind=inner resets on AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ResetTime .. ResetTime + 24h)
| extend MinutesAfterReset = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, ResetTime)
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, ResetTime, MinutesAfterReset, IPAddress, Country, ClientAppUsed, Application, AuthenticationRequirement
| order by Timestamp desc
let resets = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OperationName in ("Reset user password","Change user password","Reset password (self-service)")
| extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(TargetUpn)
| project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, TargetUpn;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ResourceDisplayName == "Office 365 Exchange Online"
| where ResultType == 0
| where AppDisplayName has_any ("Outlook","OWA","Exchange")
| join kind=inner resets on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.TargetUpn
| where TimeGenerated between (ResetTime .. ResetTime + 24h)
| extend MinutesAfterReset = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, ResetTime)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, ResetTime, MinutesAfterReset, IPAddress, Location, ClientAppUsed, AppDisplayName, AuthenticationRequirement
| order by TimeGenerated desc
First-seen OWA/Exchange sign-in from Russian IP space for a user with no RU history AICommand & Control Medium
Baselines each user's Exchange Online sign-in geography over 30 days and alerts on a first-time successful sign-in from Russian IP space, aligned to TA488/Void Blizzard attribution. Anti-join against prior RU activity keeps it low-noise versus a blanket geo block. Rationale: The campaign is attributed to Russia-aligned TA488/Void Blizzard; scoping to first-ever successful RU sign-ins against the Exchange Online resource (leftanti a 60-day RU baseline) turns a broad geo signal into a per-user first-seen anomaly on the exact resource OWAReaper abuses. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/cleaning-out-inboxes-ta488-comes-outlook-another-half-click-exploit • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/ta488-outlook-half-click-owareaper/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Employee traveling to Russia signing into webmail for the first time
  • VPN/anycast egress that geolocates to RU incorrectly
  • New hire whose first-ever sign-in happens to originate from RU (no baseline exists to compare)
  • Roaming mobile carrier that presents a Russian ASN
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the IP/ASN is genuinely Russian hosting (not a VPN/travel), and check whether the same UPN also has a recent password reset or Default-Owner folder grant. 2) Contain: if unexplained, revoke tokens, reset the password, and apply a Conditional Access block for the user; preserve the sign-in session details. 3) Hunt: sweep the RU source IP/ASN for other org users, correlate with resolutions to the four OWAReaper C2 domains, and audit mailbox folder permissions across affected users.
let RuBaseline = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp between (ago(60d) .. ago(1d))
| where Country == "RU"
| summarize by AccountUpn;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ResourceDisplayName == "Office 365 Exchange Online"
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where Country == "RU"
| join kind=leftanti RuBaseline on AccountUpn
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, ClientAppUsed, Application, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
let RuBaseline = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(60d) .. ago(1d))
| where Location == "RU"
| summarize by UserPrincipalName;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResourceDisplayName == "Office 365 Exchange Online"
| where ResultType == 0
| where Location == "RU"
| join kind=leftanti RuBaseline on UserPrincipalName
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, ClientAppUsed, AppDisplayName, UserAgent, AutonomousSystemNumber
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @network.client.geoip.country.iso_code:RU @properties.appDisplayName:(*Outlook* OR *OWA* OR *Exchange*) @properties.status.errorCode:0
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

let LookbackDays = 7d;

          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4") or SHA1 in~ ("6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4") or MD5 in~ ("6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4") or SHA1 in~ ("6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4") or MD5 in~ ("6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6897b649f29e54d8910459963bbf94ed5c7a4fe66a56bc5962540b226b8e48c4"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Recon tool reading K8s service-account token or /proc/self/environ inside a container AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts an interactive/recon binary (cat, curl, python, base64, xxd) reading the mounted Kubernetes service-account token path or /proc/self/environ inside a workload — the day-1 in-pod enumeration the article describes ('a pod reading /proc/self/environ, inspecting service-account tokens'). Distinguishes credential/environment harvesting from a normal application startup read. Rationale: Uses the article's literal strings '/proc/self/environ' and 'service-account tokens' (mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount) plus recon-tool binaries, so it fires on enumeration rather than a library's normal token read. Cross-checked the K8s SA-token-theft chain in Unit42 and TheHackerNews' breach coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/openai-agent-used-exposed-credentials.html • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/ • https://aquilax.ai/blog/kubernetes-service-account-token-theft
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1613 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Init container or entrypoint script that cats the SA token for debugging
  • CI/CD job (e.g. Helm, kubectl-in-pod) echoing token path during setup
  • Observability agent reading /proc/<pid>/environ for process metadata enrichment
  • Developer running an interactive shell in a pod during troubleshooting
  • Security scanner/CIS-benchmark tool auditing token mounts
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","containerd","dockerd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("entrypoint","docker-entrypoint","helm"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the pod/node (DeviceName), the process lineage, and whether the reader is the workload's own app or an injected shell/tool; pull the full command line and parent. 2) Contain: if the reader is not the expected app, cordon the node, kill the pod, and rotate the pod's service-account token and any secrets it could reach. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceName for subsequent connections to 169.254.169.254 (IMDS), privileged pod creation in K8s audit, and outbound to pastebin/request-capture/file-sharing services indicating C2 staging.

| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","dash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/proc/self/environ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/proc/self/environ")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Recon Tool Reading K8s Service-Account Token or Process Environ in Container
id: 8b1d2f34-6a7c-4e19-9b2a-1c4e7f0a9d21
description: Detects an interactive or recon binary reading the mounted Kubernetes service-account token path or /proc/self/environ inside a container, consistent with the Hugging Face agent breach day-1 in-pod enumeration.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/hugging-face-open-ai-breach-takeaways
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/30
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1613
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/cat'
      - '/head'
      - '/tail'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/busybox'
      - '/base64'
      - '/xxd'
      - '/strings'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount'
      - '/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount'
      - '/proc/self/environ'
  condition: selection_img and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Init containers or CI jobs that legitimately cat the service-account token for debugging
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*serviceaccount/token* OR @process.command_line:*proc/self/environ* OR @process.command_line:*secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount*) @process.name:(cat OR head OR curl OR wget OR python OR python3 OR sh OR bash OR busybox OR base64 OR xxd OR strings)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(cat|head|tail|curl|wget|python[0-9]?|sh|bash|busybox|base64|xxd|strings)$/i
| regex("(/var/run/secrets/kubernetes\\.io/serviceaccount|/run/secrets/kubernetes\\.io/serviceaccount|/proc/self/environ)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")) (Processes.process="*/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/self/environ*" OR Processes.process="*/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")) (Processes.process="*/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount*" OR Processes.process="*/proc/self/environ*" OR Processes.process="*/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Cloud instance metadata (IMDS 169.254.169.254) queried by a recon tool inside a workload AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a container-side recon binary (curl, wget, python, busybox) connecting to the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / 169.254.170.2) — the article's 'queried cloud metadata' step used to harvest node IAM credentials. Filtering on the recon tool separates credential theft from legitimate cloud-SDK IMDS calls. Rationale: Anchors on the well-known IMDS IPs (169.254.169.254 for AWS/Azure/GCP, 169.254.170.2 for ECS) paired with recon binaries, matching the article's 'queried cloud metadata' credential-harvest step while excluding in-app SDK IMDS traffic. IMDS-to-IAM abuse corroborated by Unit42/SecureByDezign. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/ • https://www.securebydezign.com/articles/kubernetes-pod-escape-cloud-takeover.html
ATT&CKT1552.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • cloud-init / bootstrap scripts curling IMDS for instance identity or user-data
  • kube2iam / kiam / IRDS sidecars that proxy IMDS via curl-like helpers
  • Health-check scripts querying instance-id or region from metadata
  • aws-cli/gcloud shell wrappers invoked by legitimate automation
  • Debugging session where an engineer manually curls IMDS
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cloud-init","user-data","kube2iam","instance-id","api-token"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the initiating process command line — did it hit the credentials path (/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ or /computeMetadata/v1/) and was IMDSv2 token flow used? Identify the host/pod and its IAM role. 2) Contain: revoke/rotate the node or pod IAM role credentials, and add a GuardDuty/SCP guardrail; if creds were retrieved, assume they are compromised and rotate. 3) Hunt: pivot to CloudTrail for AssumeRole/API calls made with those temporary credentials from a source IP outside the VPC (see UC4), and check for privileged pod creation on the same node.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","perl","ruby","nc","ncat")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2")
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound" or isempty(NetworkDirection)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fluentd aggregator pod contacts EC2 IMDS (169.254.169.254) — CVE-2026-54680 credential theft AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Fluentd aggregator (ruby/fluentd process, or a shell/curl it spawned) reaching the cloud instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254. Post-injection, @type exec is used to curl IMDS for the node's IAM role credentials, as demonstrated in the advisory's EKS 1.35 PoC. Rationale: 169.254.169.254 is the literal IMDS endpoint in the advisory's EKS PoC (curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...). A Fluentd log aggregator process reaching link-local IMDS is not normal application behaviour and indicates node-role credential theft. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/kube-logging/logging-operator/CVE-2026-54680/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1609
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS SDK/SDK-based Fluentd output plugins (e.g. S3/CloudWatch/Kinesis) that legitimately resolve IAM role creds via IMDS — verify the initiating process and command line
  • kubelet/aws-node/CNI on the node hitting IMDS (node-level, not pod-scoped)
  • IRSA-migrated clusters where an SDK still probes IMDS as a fallback
  • Monitoring/health agents co-located on the node querying instance-id
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("iam/security-credentials","/tmp/imds","instance-id") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","curl","wget")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is fluentd/ruby or a shell it spawned (not a native AWS output plugin's SDK call) and inspect the command line for /latest/meta-data or iam/security-credentials. 2) Contain: rotate the node IAM role / affected IRSA credentials, restart the aggregator pod, and block pod egress to 169.254.169.254 with a NetworkPolicy; enforce IMDSv2 hop-limit=1. 3) Hunt: search CloudTrail for the node role's AssumeRole/API usage from unexpected IPs and pivot to UC 'Fluentd spawns shell' and any external egress from the pod.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ruby","fluentd","fluent","sh","bash","dash","curl","wget")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound" or isempty(NetworkDirection)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fluentd/ruby aggregator spawns a shell or network tool (@type exec RCE) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Fluentd aggregator process (ruby/fluentd) spawning /bin/sh, curl, wget, nc or an interpreter — the observable side effect of the injected @type exec plugin flushing its buffer and running an arbitrary command (e.g. /bin/sh -c "id > /tmp/pwned") per CVE-2026-54680. Rationale: The advisory PoC executes /bin/sh -c "id > /tmp/pwned" via the injected out_exec plugin; Fluentd runs on ruby, so a ruby/fluentd parent spawning a shell or curl is the direct RCE observable. out_exec normally shells out only for legitimate configured commands, which are rare and known. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h • https://docs.fluentd.org/output/exec
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1609
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimately configured Fluentd out_exec / exec_filter output that shells out to a known helper script
  • Fluentd plugin install or entrypoint scripts invoking sh during pod startup
  • Ruby-based sidecars unrelated to Fluentd that share the 'ruby' process name on the node
  • Liveness/readiness exec probes running sh inside the fluentd container
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/pwned","169.254.169.254","id >","/dev/tcp/","bash -i","curl -sS")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child command line — /tmp/pwned, id, curl to IMDS, reverse-shell, or unknown binaries confirm abuse vs a sanctioned out_exec command; capture the aggregator pod and node. 2) Contain: kill the aggregator pod, remove the injected Flow/Output CRD, and reload clean config; snapshot the pod filesystem for IR. 3) Hunt: enumerate all Flow/ClusterFlow/Output objects for @type exec, review command output artifacts under /tmp, and correlate with IMDS and external-egress UCs on the same host/time window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ruby","fluentd","fluent")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("ruby","fluentd","fluent")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/curl","/wget","/nc","/ncat","/python")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fluentd aggregator pod external egress to public internet (post-RCE C2/exfil) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections to public (non-cluster, non-RFC1918) IPs initiated by the Fluentd aggregator process (ruby/fluentd) or a shell/interpreter it spawned. After @type exec RCE, this surfaces broader C2 or data exfiltration beyond the IMDS pivot already covered. Rationale: The advisory's impact is arbitrary command execution in the shared aggregator; the same out_exec primitive that curls IMDS can reach any external host for C2/exfil. Scoping to fluentd/ruby (and children) egressing to public IPs — excluding cluster/RFC1918/IMDS ranges — isolates the anomalous post-RCE network behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/kube-logging/logging-operator/CVE-2026-54680/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Fluentd output plugins legitimately shipping logs to a public SaaS/managed aggregator (Datadog, Elastic Cloud, Loki, S3 over public endpoint)
  • Plugin/gem installation at pod startup pulling from rubygems.org / PyPI
  • Node-level package or telemetry agents sharing process names
  • DNS-over-HTTPS or update checks by co-resident tooling
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteIP in ("and-known-saas-output-endpoints")) // maintain an allowlist of sanctioned public log-shipping destinations for this cluster
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate the distinct public destinations per fluentd host and compare against the sanctioned log-shipping/output endpoints for this cluster; unfamiliar IPs/ports (esp. shell/curl-initiated) are suspect. 2) Contain: apply an egress NetworkPolicy restricting the aggregator to approved destinations, restart the pod, and remove any injected Flow/Output CRDs. 3) Hunt: correlate the destination IPs with threat intel, review bytes-out for exfil volume, and pivot to the shell-spawn and CRD-injection UCs to confirm the RCE root cause.

Prebid-server SSRF payload in OpenRTB2 auction request parameters AIExploitation Low
Hunts inbound requests to prebid-server's /openrtb2/ endpoints carrying bidder-adapter host/subdomain parameters that resolve to internal, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata destinations. This targets CVE-2026-54735 at the parameter layer — catching the crafted host value before it triggers an outbound forged request. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact mechanism — bidder parameters interpolated into outbound URLs — plus prebid's documented /openrtb2/ endpoints and the canonical SSRF targets (169.254.169.254 metadata IP, RFC1918, loopback). Confidence is Low/FP high because most adapter params ride in the POST JSON body, so this fires cleanly only where the WAF/app tier logs request bodies or GET-style params. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54735 • https://docs.prebid.org/prebid-server/endpoints/openrtb2/pbs-endpoint-auction.html • https://docs.prebid.org/dev-docs/pbs-bidders.html
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate bidder params that embed geo/region tokens resembling private IP octets (e.g. '10' region codes)
  • Internal QA/load testing pointing an adapter at a staging endpoint on a private IP
  • Security scanners (Burp/Nessus) probing /openrtb2/ with SSRF payloads during an authorized test
  • Load-balancer or uptime monitors hitting /openrtb2/ health probes
  • CDN/WAF appending internal origin hostnames into the logged URL
Suppression filter
| where not(RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus","Burp","Nuclei","zgrab")) and SourceIP !startswith "10."
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body/URL and identify which bidder adapter param carried the internal/metadata host; confirm the source IP is external and not a known scanner/QA range. 2) Contain: if prebid-server < v4.4.0, disable the abused dynamic-hostname adapter (article workaround) and block the source IP at the WAF; prioritize patching to v4.4.0. 3) Hunt: correlate the request timestamp with UC 'Outbound anomaly' and 'Metadata theft' hunts on the same prebid host to confirm whether a forged outbound request actually fired.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/openrtb2/"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(169\.254\.169\.254|169\.254\.170\.2|metadata\.google\.internal|127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|0\.0\.0\.0|10\.[0-9]|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Prebid-server OpenRTB2 SSRF Payload in Request URL
id: 6f2b1c84-7d1e-4a2b-9d3f-2b7a1c9e4d51
description: Detects requests to prebid-server /openrtb2/ endpoints whose URL contains internal, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata host values indicative of CVE-2026-54735 SSRF exploitation.

Prebid-server outbound requests to internal ranges / internal host fan-out (SSRF) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the prebid-server process making outbound connections into RFC1918 / link-local space, and in particular fanning out to many distinct internal hosts within a short window — the observable server-side effect of CVE-2026-54735 being used to reach internal services or scan the network. Rationale: The article's core impact is 'HTTP requests to unintended destinations ... exposing internal network services.' Rather than an allowlist of bad ranges, this baselines the prebid-server process's normal peers and alerts on previously-unseen internal peers plus a fan-out threshold — the network shape of SSRF-driven internal reach/scanning. Anchored to the concrete process name 'prebid-server'. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://docs.prebid.org/dev-docs/pbs-bidders.html
ATT&CKT1046 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • prebid-server legitimately calling internal Prebid Cache / analytics services over private IPs
  • East-west container-to-container traffic in a Kubernetes/service-mesh deployment inflating distinct-dest counts
  • Internal ad-exchange peering reached over a private interconnect
  • Monitoring/health-check agents co-located with the origin host
  • Blue/green or autoscaling events where new internal cache endpoints appear and trip the baseline anti-join
Suppression filter
| where not(Dests has_any ("prebidcache"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the destinations — are they known Prebid Cache/analytics hosts or unexpected infra (DBs, admin consoles, hypervisor mgmt)? Check the port spread (scan-like sequential ports vs one service port). 2) Contain: isolate/patch the prebid host to v4.4.0 and add an egress policy limiting prebid-server to approved bidder/cache CIDRs. 3) Hunt: pivot to the metadata-theft UC on the same host and to inbound /openrtb2/ requests immediately preceding the outbound burst to identify the triggering bid request.
let Baseline = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "prebid-server"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Private"
    | summarize by RemoteIP;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "prebid-server"
| where RemoteIPType == "Private"
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on RemoteIP
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), DistinctInternalDests=dcount(RemoteIP), Ports=make_set(RemotePort,20), Dests=make_set(RemoteIP,50) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where DistinctInternalDests >= 5   // 5 previously-unseen internal peers in 24h = SSRF-driven reach/scan
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) or DstIpAddr startswith "169.254."
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctInternalDests=dcount(DstIpAddr), Ports=make_set(DstPortNumber,20), Dests=make_set(DstIpAddr,50) by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where DistinctInternalDests >= 10   // internal host fan-out from a single origin in 10m = scan-like
| order by FirstSeen desc

| stats dc(dest) as distinct_internal_dests dc(dest_port) as distinct_ports values(dest) as dests min(_time) as firstTime by src
| where distinct_internal_dests >= 10
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Prebid-server access to cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254) via SSRF AIActions on Objectives Medium
High-fidelity alert on the prebid-server process connecting to the cloud instance metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / 169.254.170.2), and a companion CloudTrail hunt for instance-role credentials being used from off-instance IPs — the credential-theft path implied by 'host environment data extraction' in CVE-2026-54735. Rationale: The article title/body call out 'host environment data extraction'; the canonical realization of SSRF on a cloud host is a request to 169.254.169.254 to steal the instance role. Scoping to InitiatingProcessFileName == 'prebid-server' makes the endpoint side high-fidelity, and the CloudTrail companion catches the stolen role token being replayed from an external IP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54735 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/
ATT&CKT1552.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • prebid-server using the AWS/GCP SDK default credential chain, which legitimately queries IMDS at startup for region/role
  • IMDSv2 token fetch (PUT /latest/api/token) issued by an embedded SDK during normal operation
  • Sidecar/agent frameworks bundled in the container image reading instance identity
  • Autoscaling re-launch causing a burst of legitimate first-start IMDS calls
  • CloudTrail AssumedRole calls from a NAT-gateway public IP misclassified as off-instance
Suppression filter
| where RemotePort != 80 or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--aws-region"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the IMDS hit correlates with process startup (often legit SDK) or with runtime bid traffic (suspicious); capture the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and any preceding inbound /openrtb2/ request. 2) Contain: if unexpected, revoke/rotate the instance role credentials immediately, enforce IMDSv2 with hop-limit 1, and patch to v4.4.0. 3) Hunt: run the CloudTrail companion for the instance role's session issuer used from external IPs, and review STS AssumeRole/GetSessionToken and any new IAM/S3 actions in the following hour.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "prebid-server"
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Prebid-server SSRF filter-bypass via encoded internal host in request AIExploitation Low
Hunts /openrtb2/ requests whose parameters use URL/double-URL/hex/decimal-IP encoding to smuggle an internal or metadata host past naive input filters — the obfuscated variant of the CVE-2026-54735 SSRF payload. Rationale: The advisory notes the flaw is 'without proper input validation' and the v4.4.0 fix prohibits certain hostname characters — implying attackers will encode payloads to slip past filters. Patterns target the well-known SSRF encodings for 169.254.169.254/127.0.0.1 (double-encoding %25, encoded octets %31%36%39, decimal 2852039166, octal 017700000001, hex 0x). Low confidence because it depends on request-body/query logging and encoded strings are inherently noisy. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54735
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimately URL-encoded creative/macro parameters in bid requests
  • Analytics/tracking URLs passed as encoded params by adapters
  • Double-encoding introduced by an upstream CDN or proxy normalization
  • Base64 creative blobs that coincidentally contain '0x' or long hex runs
  • Automated scanners fuzzing the endpoint with encoded payloads during authorized testing
Suppression filter
| where not(RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus","Burp","Nuclei","zgrab"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: URL-decode the flagged parameter (one or two passes) and determine the final host it resolves to — internal/metadata means true positive. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, disable the abused dynamic-hostname adapter, and patch to v4.4.0 (which strips disallowed hostname characters). 3) Hunt: check the same source IP for the plaintext SSRF UC and pivot to the prebid host's outbound/metadata UCs to see if any encoded attempt succeeded in firing a forged request.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/openrtb2/"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(%25[0-9a-f]{2}|%32%35%34|%31%36%39|%6d%65%74%61|0x[0-9a-f]{6,}|2852039166|017700000001|127%2e0%2e0%2e1|169%2e254)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-20316 — Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Use of Hard-coded Password Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-07-29 1 use case 0 techniques 2 kill-chain phases detected

Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) formerly known as Firepower Management Center contains a use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account to access sensitive data within the impacted systems. Vendor: Cisco, Product: Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC). Federal patch due: 2026-08-01.
